title: Inquirers' Showcase
topic: Write a puzzle with one answer, check a friend's puzzle, and teach an idea

items.q: I am a number. I am 4 more than 11. What number am I?

slips.say: That is 11 take away 4. More means we add.

tpl.q: I am a number. I am {a} more than {b}. What number am I?

items.q: Two numbers add up to 12. One number is 2 more than the other. What is the smaller number?
items.hint: List the pairs that make 12. Find the pair that is 2 apart.
steps: The pairs are 5 and 7, 4 and 8, and so on.
5 and 7 make 12, and 7 is 2 more than 5.

slips.say: That is the bigger number. Which number is smaller?

tpl.q: Two numbers add up to {t}. One number is {d} more than the other. What is the smaller number?
tpl.hint: List the pairs that make {t}. Find the pair that is {d} apart.
steps: Find the pair that is {d} apart.

items.q: Which one is a good puzzle?
items.hint: A good puzzle has a story, numbers and one question.
steps: A good puzzle has a story, numbers and one question.
The second one has all three.
items.answer: Ali has 5 pens. Mei has 3 more pens than Ali. How many pens does Mei have?

a: How many pens does Mei have?
slips.say: That is only a question. A good puzzle has a story and numbers too.

options: Ali has 5 pens. Mei has 3 more pens than Ali. How many pens does Mei have?
How many pens does Mei have?

items.q: A child writes: Write a number between 1 and 9. Does this puzzle have exactly one answer?
steps: Many numbers fit, so it does not have exactly one answer.

slips.say: Try two different numbers. Do both fit?

items.q: Mei thinks of a number. She takes away 5 and gets 9. What is her number?

slips.say: That is 9 take away 5. Work backwards: add the 5.

tpl.q: Mei thinks of a number. She takes away {a} and gets {r}. What is her number?

items.q: How many whole numbers are bigger than 5 and smaller than 11?

slips.say: Do not count 5 or 11. Bigger than 5 starts at 6.

tpl.q: How many whole numbers are bigger than {a} and smaller than {b}?
tpl.hint: List them. Do not count {a} or {b}.

items.q: A child writes: Two numbers add up to 10. One is 4 more than the other. The numbers are 6 and 4. What is wrong?
steps: 6 and 4 add up to 10. That clue fits.
The second clue does not fit.

a: 6 and 4 do not add up to 10
slips.say: 6 and 4 do make 10. Check the other clue.

options: 6 and 4 do not add up to 10

items.q: A child in another class writes 8 + 6 = 15. What is the right answer?
items.hint: Add again, or check by taking away.
steps: 6 take away 2 is 4, and 10 and 4 make 14.

slips.say: That is the wrong answer the child wrote.

tpl.q: A child in another class writes {a} + {b} = {w}. What is the right answer?
tpl.hint: Add again, or check by taking away.

items.q: Two numbers add up to 14. One number is 4 more than the other. What is the bigger number?
items.hint: List the pairs that make 14. Find the pair that is 4 apart.
steps: The pairs are 5 and 9, 6 and 8, and so on.
5 and 9 make 14, and 9 is 4 more than 5.

slips.say: That is the smaller number. Which number is bigger?

tpl.q: Two numbers add up to {t}. One number is {d} more than the other. What is the bigger number?
tpl.hint: List the pairs that make {t}. Find the pair that is {d} apart.
steps: Find the pair that is {d} apart.

items.q: How many different pairs of whole numbers add up to 9? Count 0 and 9 as a pair. Do not count the same pair twice.
items.hint: List the pairs in order: 0 and 9, 1 and 8, and so on.
steps: 5 and 4 is the same pair as 4 and 5.

slips.say: That counts 4 and 5 and 5 and 4 as two pairs. Count each pair once.

tpl.q: How many different pairs of whole numbers add up to {t}? Count 0 and {t} as a pair. Do not count the same pair twice.
tpl.hint: List the pairs in order: 0 and {t}, 1 and the next, and so on.
steps: List the pairs in order, starting with 0 and {t}.
Stop when the pairs start to repeat.

items.q: Write your own puzzle with a rule. Check that it has exactly one answer, and show why.
items.hint: Use two numbers. List every case.
steps: Write a rule and two numbers.
Check there is exactly one answer.

items.q: A week after the 5th is which date? Write the number.
steps: A week after the 5th is the 12th.

slips.say: 7 is the days in a week. Add them to the date.

tpl.q: A week after the {a|ord} is which date? Write the number.
steps: A week after the {a|ord} is the {ans|ord}.

items.q: How many days are in 2 weeks?
items.hint: One week is 7 days. Count in 7s.

slips.say: 2 is the number of weeks. Count the days: 7 for each week.

tpl.q: How many days are in {w} weeks?
tpl.hint: One week is 7 days. Count in 7s.
